title: File handling
test_conventions: Learner code runs first in a fresh namespace. Each test is a Python snippet (assert statements) executed afterwards in the same namespace; the learner's printed output is available to tests as the string variable __stdout__. expected_output comparisons are exact after stripping trailing whitespace on every line. No input(), network or pip. Files may be created in the working directory (an in-memory file system in the browser); use unique file names. The learner's source code is available to tests as the string variable __source__ (use it with ast or substring checks to reject hard-coded answers).

worked_example.code:
with open('notes19.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write('line one\nline two')
with open('notes19.txt') as f:
    print(f.read().splitlines())
notes: with open(...) as f closes the file for you when the block ends.
read().splitlines() gives the lines without the newline characters.
notes_tr: with open(...) as f blok bitince dosyayı senin için kapatır.
read().splitlines() satırları satır sonu karakterleri olmadan verir.

exercises.code:
with open('demo19a.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write('This is an example\nSecond line')
with open('demo19a.txt') as f:
    print(f.read(7))
with open('demo19a.txt') as f:
    print(f.readlines())
with open('demo19a.txt') as f:
    print(f.read().splitlines())
choices:
This is an example
['This is an example', 'Second line']
['This is an example', 'Second line']

This is
['This is an example', 'Second line']
['This is an example', 'Second line']

This is
['This is an example\n', 'Second line']
['This is an example', 'Second line']
exercises.expected_output:
This is
['This is an example\n', 'Second line']
['This is an example', 'Second line']
exercises.explanation: read(7) returns the first 7 characters: 'This is'. readlines() returns the lines WITH their '\n' endings. read().splitlines() returns the lines without line endings.

misconceptions.This is an example\n['This is an example: read(7) reads only 7 characters, not a whole line.
misconceptions.This is\n['This is an example', 'Second: readlines() keeps the newline character at the end of each line except possibly the last; splitlines() removes it.

exercises.explanation_tr: read(7) ilk 7 karakteri verir: 'This is'. readlines() satırları '\n' sonlarıyla birlikte verir. read().splitlines() ise satırları satır sonları olmadan verir.

misconceptions_tr.This is an example\n['This is an example: read(7) tüm bir satırı değil, sadece 7 karakter okur.
misconceptions_tr.This is\n['This is an example', 'Second: readlines() her satırın sonundaki satır sonu karakterini korur (son satır hariç olabilir); splitlines() onu kaldırır.

worked_example.code:
import json
person = {'name': 'Asabeneh', 'city': 'Helsinki'}
text = json.dumps(person)
print(text)
print(json.loads(text)['city'])
notes: json.dumps turns a dictionary into JSON text; json.loads turns JSON text into a dictionary.
JSON text always uses double quotes.
notes_tr: json.dumps sözlüğü JSON metnine, json.loads JSON metnini sözlüğe çevirir.
JSON metni her zaman çift tırnak kullanır.

exercises.code:
import json
person = {'name': 'Asabeneh', 'skills': ['Python', 'React']}
text = json.dumps(person)
print(type(text).__name__)
print(text)
back = json.loads(text)
print(back['skills'][0])
exercises.explanation: json.dumps returns a str. JSON text uses double quotes, with a space after each colon and comma. json.loads gives the dictionary back, so back['skills'][0] is 'Python'.

misconceptions.dict\n{'name': 'Asabeneh', 'skills': ['P: dumps returns a STRING, and JSON uses double quotes.
misconceptions.str\n{\"name\": \"Asabeneh\", \"skills\": back['skills'] is a list; index 0 is its first item.

exercises.explanation_tr: json.dumps bir str döndürür. JSON metni çift tırnak kullanır; iki noktadan ve virgülden sonra boşluk bırakır. json.loads sözlüğü geri verir, yani back['skills'][0] 'Python' olur.

misconceptions_tr.dict\n{'name': 'Asabeneh', 'skills': ['P: dumps bir STRING döndürür ve JSON çift tırnak kullanır.
misconceptions_tr.str\n{\"name\": \"Asabeneh\", \"skills\": back['skills'] bir listedir; 0. indeks ilk elemanıdır.

worked_example.code:
import csv, io
data = 'name,city\nAsab,Helsinki\n'
rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(data)))
print(rows)
notes: csv.reader gives one list per row; the header is just the first row.
io.StringIO lets csv read from a string as if it were a file.
notes_tr: csv.reader her satır için bir liste verir; başlık sadece ilk satırdır.
io.StringIO, csv'nin bir metni dosyaymış gibi okumasını sağlar.

exercises.code:
import csv, io
data = '"name","country","city"\n"Asabeneh","Finland","Helsinki"\n"Lidiya","Norway","Oslo"\n'
rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(data)))
print(rows[0])
print(len(rows))
print(rows[2][2])
exercises.explanation: csv.reader splits each line into a list and removes the quotes. The header is rows[0]; with two data rows there are 3 rows. rows[2] is Lidiya's row and its index 2 is the city: Oslo.

misconceptions.['name', 'country', 'city']\n2\nOslo: The header row is also a row, so there are 3 rows in total.
misconceptions.['Asabeneh', 'Finland', 'Helsinki']\n3\n: rows[0] is the FIRST row of the file, which is the header.

exercises.explanation_tr: csv.reader her satırı bir listeye böler ve tırnakları kaldırır. Başlık rows[0]'dır; iki veri satırıyla toplam 3 satır olur. rows[2] Lidiya'nın satırıdır ve 2. indeks şehirdir: Oslo.

misconceptions_tr.['name', 'country', 'city']\n2\nOslo: Başlık satırı da bir satırdır, yani toplam 3 satır var.
misconceptions_tr.['Asabeneh', 'Finland', 'Helsinki']\n3\n: rows[0] dosyanın İLK satırıdır, o da başlıktır.

hints: io.StringIO(text) lets csv read a string like a file.
The first row gives the keys; zip it with each later row.
return [dict(___(header, row)) for row in rows[1:]] (which function pairs two lists?)

solution.approach: Read all rows, take the first as the header and zip it with every other row.
solution.code:
import csv
import io

def csv_to_dicts(text):
    rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(text)))
    header = rows[0]
    return [dict(zip(header, row)) for row in rows[1:]]
solution.approach_tr: Tüm satırları oku, ilkini başlık yap ve diğer her satırla eşleştir.

hints_tr: io.StringIO(text) csv'nin string'i dosya gibi okumasını sağlar.

return [dict(___(header, row)) for row in rows[1:]] (iki listeyi eşleştiren fonksiyon hangisi?)

tests.failure_message: Read the column of the CSV text you are given; do not hard-code results.
tests.failure_message_tr: Verilen CSV metninin sütununu oku; sonuçları elle yazma.

hints: Find the column's position in the header row first.
Look the column name up in the header list to get its position.
position = rows[0].___(column) (which list method gives the position of an item?)

solution.approach: Locate the column in the header, then collect that position from every data row.
solution.code:
import csv
import io

def column_values(text, column):
    rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(text)))
    position = rows[0].index(column)
    return [row[position] for row in rows[1:]]
solution.approach_tr: Sütunu başlıkta bul, sonra her veri satırından o konumu topla.

hints: Run it: what is printed? It is an Element object, not the text.

solution.approach: find returns the Element itself. Use .text to get the text it contains.
solution.code:
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
xml_text = '<person><name>Asabeneh</name><city>Helsinki</city></person>'
root = ET.fromstring(xml_text)
print(root.find('city').text)
solution.approach_tr: find, Element'in kendisini döndürür. İçindeki metin için .text kullan.

exercises.prompt: In your own words: why is 'with open(...) as f' better than calling open() and close() yourself?
exercises.prompt_tr: Kendi cümlelerinizle: 'with open(...) as f' neden open() ve close() çağırmaktan daha iyidir?
exercises.model_answer: A with block closes the file automatically when the block ends, even if an error happens inside it. With a manual close() it is easy to forget it or skip it after an error, which can leave the file open or the data unsaved.
exercises.model_answer_tr: with bloğu, blok bitince dosyayı otomatik olarak kapatır; içeride bir hata olsa bile. close()'u elle çağırırsan onu unutmak ya da bir hatadan sonra atlamak kolaydır; bu da dosyanın açık kalmasına ya da verinin kaydedilmemesine yol açabilir.
